Caveat: official stats (citypopulation.de) track only مركز الفاو, and a 2023 stats report lists only مركز الفاو — the subdistrict status of البحار/الخليج العربي may reflect older or lagging official data.

Formerly ناحية طلحة of Al-Midaina district; elevated to independent district ~2019 (ar.wiki article titled قضاء الإمام الصادق). No subdistricts; 2024 census population 113,517. A 2025 Basra University study notes Ministry of Planning/Health data still aggregates it under Al-Midaina.
ناحية سفوان elevated to district (21 Jan 2024); ناحية خور الزبير created the same day (Jan 2024). Remaining subdistricts: أم قصر and خور الزبير.
Formerly ناحية سفوان of Al-Zubair district; elevated to district 21 Jan 2024 (Minister of Planning approval, ar.wiki قضاء سفوان). Comprises 11 مقاطعة; no formal subdistricts.

Five نواحي per current ar.wiki قضاء شط العرب infobox: التنومة، الفيحاء، النشوة، الكباسي، عتبة (ناحية الفيحاء independently confirmed as a ناحية of the district). Official stats only track مركز شط العرب + النشوة; التنومة/الفيحاء/الكباسي/عتبة appear to be newer additions.

governorates.notes: District list follows the most current official scheme (11 districts) per citypopulation.de's 2024-census data and the ar.wiki 'أقضية العراق' list (10; missing only Aṣ-Ṣādiq). English Wikipedia's Basra Governorate article is outdated: it lists only 8 districts (missing Al-Haritha, As-Sadiq, Safwan) and ar.wiki's محافظة البصرة article still lists 9. Subdistricts verified from current ar.wiki district articles and confirmed where possible: As-Siba (Abu Al-Khaseeb), At-Tanuma/Al-Fayha/An-Nashwa/Al-Kabasi/Ataba (Shatt Al-Arab), Al-Imam Al-Qaim (Al-Qurna), Izz ad-Din Salim (Al-Midaina), Umm Qasr + Khor Az-Zubayr (Al-Zubair), Al-Faw + Al-Bihar + Al-Khalij Al-Arabi (Al-Faw). Official stats (citypopulation.de subdistrict table, still the older scheme) agree on As-Siba, An-Nashwa, Ath-Thughir (=Al-Imam Al-Qaim), Izz ad-Din Salim and Umm Qasr, but do not track the newer subdistricts (Khor Az-Zubayr, Al-Fayha, At-Tanuma, Al-Kabasi, Ataba) nor the Faw subdistricts البحار/الخليج العربي — possible lag in official data; flagged per district.

governorates.notes: District count discrepancy: English Wikipedia ('Maysan Governorate', 'Districts of Iraq') lists 6 districts, but citypopulation.de's admin table (2024 census), ar.wikipedia's Kumayt article, and the 2018 Maysan governor's office announcement all confirm Kumayt (كميت) was elevated from a nahiya of Amara district to its own district (قضاء كميت), giving 7 districts. Using the most current (7-district) list. Subdistrict Arabic spellings verified against ar.wikipedia 'قائمة نواحي العراق'. Subdistrict lists include the district center (مركز قضاء), which official Iraqi stats count as a second-level unit alongside nahiyas; 8 nahiyas proper + 7 centers = 15 entries. In 2018 Maysan also created two new nahiyas (البتيرة، نهر سعد) but no source I could access places them under a specific district, so they are omitted. Kumayt's internal nahiya structure could not be verified (only its center is listed).

governorates.notes: Sources used: ar.wikipedia 'أقضية العراق' (current; lists 13 districts), ar.wikipedia 'محافظة ذي قار' (2022 admin table; 8 districts, mixed/outdated), individual ar.wikipedia district articles, thiqar.gov.iq official announcements (~2019 and 2026), nasiriaelc.com reports of IHEC/Ministry of Planning approvals (2018–2019), citypopulation.de (COSIT 2018 estimate snapshot), en.wikipedia 'Dhi Qar Governorate' and 'Districts of Iraq'. DISCREPANCIES: en.wikipedia lists only 6 districts and 'Districts of Iraq' only 5 — both reflect the pre-2014 structure and are outdated. citypopulation.de lists 10 (2018 COSIT snapshot): Ad-Dawayah, Al-Fuhud, Al-Islah, Al-Jibayish, An-Nasiriyah, Ar-Rifa'i, Ash-Shatrah, Qal'at Sikar, Sa'id Dakhil, Suq ash-Shuyukh — it misses al-Gharraf, al-Fajr, al-Nasr, al-Batha'a and Karmat Bani Sa'id. The 2022 ar.wiki admin table lists 8 (Nasiriyah, Shatrah, al-Rifa'i, Suq al-Shuyukh, al-Jibayish, al-Nasr, al-Fajr, al-Fuhud) and re-treats al-Islah, Sayyid Dakhil, al-Gharraf, Qal'at Sukkar and al-Dawaya as subdistricts, contradicting their 2014–2019 Ministry-approved district status. The current ar.wiki 'Aqdia al-Iraq' list (13) omits Sayyid Dakhil and al-Islah — almost certainly wiki incompleteness, as both are confirmed districts by official sources through 2026. One academic paper (~2024) still calls al-Fuhud a nahiya of al-Jibayish and Karmat Bani Sa'id a nahiya of Suq al-Shuyukh — outdated relative to the 2018/2019 upgrades. A proposed Qada'a al-Ukaikah (2019 planning document) could not be confirmed as finalized and is not listed. Subdistrict lists reflect the post-upgrade structure; single-unit new districts are reported with empty lists and explanatory notes.

governorates.notes: Muthanna's district structure has expanded beyond the older 5-district layout (Samawah, Rumaitha, Khidhir, Salman, Warka). Four former subdistricts were upgraded to districts: Warka (already a district in citypopulation.de's 2018 data), Suwair and Hilal (Iraqi Ministry of Planning approval reported by Iraqi News Agency INA ~2025, cited in ar.wikipedia's Rumaitha District article), Najmi (listed as a district in ar.wikipedia's Muthanna admin table, mid-2026), and Majd (named as a district by Governor Muhannad al-Attabi, iraqpaper.com 2026-08-31). Current official structure: 9 districts + 3 subdistricts (Karama under Warka, Daraji under Khidhir, Busaiyah under Salman) = 12 units, matching the old 5+7 count. Discrepancies: ar.wikipedia's infobox says 8 districts/3 subdistricts and its admin table still lists Majd as Rumaitha's subdistrict (likely edited before the Majd upgrade); the governor's Aug-2026 statement lists 8 districts (incl. Majd) + 3 subdistricts = 11 units but omits Samawah district, presumably because that land-title event did not cover the provincial-center district; muthana.gov.iq still describes Majd as a Rumaitha subdistrict (stale). en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq' still lists only 4 Muthanna districts (Al-Khidhir, Al-Rumaitha, Al-Salman, Al-Samawa) - outdated; en.wikipedia 'Muthanna Governorate' has no district list. Confirmed: Afak, Diwaniya and Hamza belong to Qadisiyyah Governorate (per 'Districts of Iraq' and citypopulation.de) and are NOT in Muthanna. Each district's subdistrict list below includes its central subdistrict (same name as the district), following citypopulation.de's 'Central Subdistrict' convention and ar.wikipedia's admin table.

governorates.notes: Current official structure is 13 districts + 3 subdistricts (16 units), per citypopulation.de Iraq admin page (2024 census data) and a 2026 University of Al-Qadisiyah journal paper (مجلة القادسية للعلوم الإنسانية), which explicitly assigns the only remaining subdistricts: Nafar (Afaq district), Al-Salahiyah (Shamiya), Al-Bassamiya (Hamza). Recent Iraqi news corroborates district status for Shanafiya, Sudayr, Shafi'iyah, Al-Budair, and Hamza Al-Sharqi. Older sources (ar.wikipedia governorate article — still not updated; en.wikipedia 'Districts of Iraq'; IOM 2009 profile) list only 4 districts (Diwaniya, Al-Shamiya, Afaq, Hamza) with 11 subdistricts — the other 9 districts are former subdistricts that were upgraded. Discrepancies: (1) citypopulation.de lists the Daghara district as 'Akad [Ad-Daghārah]' (native اكد) — uncorroborated anywhere else, so الدغارة retained; (2) ar.wikipedia's قضاء الحمزة article title uses 'Al-Hamza' but its text and 2025 Iraqi news use the official name الحمزة الشرقي (Hamza Al-Sharqi); (3) Al-Budair is also written آل بدير. kur fields intentionally empty — no Kurdish names used for this governorate.

governorates.notes: Sources: en.wikipedia 'Wasit Governorate' and 'Districts of Iraq' (both still show the OLD 6-district structure: Kut, Suwaira, Aziziyah, Hay, Numaniya, Badra); ar.wikipedia 'قائمة نواحي العراق' and 'أقضية العراق' show the CURRENT 9-district structure (الموفقية, الأحرار, الزبيدية elevated from subdistricts to districts; Al-Ahrar upgrade confirmed 27/2/2019 per Iraqi Ministry of Planning letter 4692); ar.wikipedia 'محافظة واسط' infobox says 9 districts/9 subdistricts though its admin table still shows the old 6-district layout. citypopulation.de (2018 data) reflects the old structure and was used only to cross-check Arabic spellings of older subdistricts. New subdistricts per the subdistrict list: ناحية القصبة القديمة (الدجيلي) under Kut and ناحية سيد الشهداء under Aziziyah. Districts of Numaniya, Ahrar, Muwafaqiyah, Zubaidiyah have no subdistricts (district-center only) in the sources.
